original_question: If A and B are approximately amenable Banach algebras, must their projective tensor product A \hat{\otimes} B be approximately amenable? Likewise, if A and B are pseudo-amenable Banach algebras, must A \hat{\otimes} B be pseudo-amenable?
target_in_paper: Question 7 in §3.2 ("Direct sum and tensor product"): "Is A \hat{\otimes} B approximately amenable (resp. pseudo-amenable) if both A and B are?" ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact tensor-product permanence issue the paper asks about: the projective tensor product, the two properties involved (approximate amenability and pseudo-amenability), and the implication from the two factors to the tensor product. It is essentially Question 7 in §3.2, just spelled out in two sentences instead of the paper’s single parenthetical formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
missing_details: State explicitly that A and B are Banach algebras; the whole discussion is in that category, and Question 7 is posed there. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

Specify that A \hat{\otimes} B means the Banach-space projective tensor product, equipped with the natural Banach-algebra product; §1 introduces this tensor-product setting when discussing diagonals and approximate diagonals. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
Make clear that this is an open question in the paper, not a proved theorem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

Do not add extra hypotheses absent from the official formulation, such as bounded approximate identities, separability, amenability of one factor, or bounded pseudo-contractibility; the nearby text mentions such stronger hypotheses only as partial results, not as part of Question 7 itself. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

For full stand-alone readability, one should either define or explicitly invoke the paper’s meanings of “approximately amenable” (Definition 1.2) and “pseudo-amenable” (Definition 1.3). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
refined_question: Let A and B be Banach algebras, and let A \hat{\otimes} B denote their Banach-space projective tensor product endowed with the canonical algebra multiplication. Is A \hat{\otimes} B approximately amenable (respectively, pseudo-amenable) whenever both A and B are approximately amenable (respectively, pseudo-amenable)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
justification: The draft is targeting the exact official problem in the paper: after recalling a previously known tensor-product result under stronger assumptions and then proving Theorem 3.7 for boundedly pseudo-contractible algebras, Zhang asks in §3.2 whether approximate amenability or pseudo-amenability of both factors passes to A \hat{\otimes} B. The introduction supplies the meanings of the two properties through Definition 1.2 (approximately amenable) and Definition 1.3 (pseudo-amenable). So the sharp paper-faithful rewrite is the unqualified permanence question for the projective tensor product, with no added bounded approximate identity, amenability, separability, or contractibility assumptions. EuDML confirms the published article span as pp. 441-454. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
